classification.difficultyReason: Equate two parabola expressions, handle cancellation or factorisation, recover intersection coordinates, and coordinate both curves' vertices and intercepts in one sketch.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of each of the following pairs of equations, labelling their points of intersection.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=(x-2)^2\\x^2&=x^2-4x+4\\4x&=4\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitution gives $y=1^2=1$, so the intersection is $(1,1)$.

Both parabolas open upwards. Their vertices and axial intercepts are $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$ respectively; the second parabola also has $y$-intercept $(0,4)$.

spec.description: Two upward parabolas with vertices at zero and two; label their intersection and axial intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-x^2&=-(x+3)^2\\-x^2&=-x^2-6x-9\\6x&=-9\\x&=-\frac32\end{align*}$$
Substitution gives $y=-(-\frac32)^2=-\frac94$.

Both parabolas open downwards. Their vertices and $x$-intercepts are $(0,0)$ and $(-3,0)$ respectively. The second has $y$-intercept $(0,-9)$.

spec.description: Two downward parabolas, including both vertices, their intersection and the second y-intercept.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2&=(x-1)^2\\x^2+2x+1&=x^2-2x+1\\4x&=0\\x&=0\end{align*}$$
Substitution gives $y=(0+1)^2=1$.

Both parabolas open upwards. Their vertices and $x$-intercepts are $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ respectively; both have $y$-intercept $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Upward parabolas symmetric about x=-1 and x=1, meeting on the y-axis.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=-x(x-1)\\2x^2-x&=0\\x(2x-1)&=0\\x&=0,\ \frac12\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $y=x^2$ gives $y=0,\ \frac14$ respectively.

The first parabola opens upwards with vertex $(0,0)$. The second opens downwards, has intercepts $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$, and vertex $(\frac12,\frac14)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola and downward parabola meeting at the origin and at the latter's vertex.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-1&=-x^2+2\\2x^2&=3\\x^2&=\frac32\\x&=\pm\sqrt{\frac32}\end{align*}$$
Substitution gives $y=\frac32-1=\frac12$ for both values.

The upward parabola has vertex $(0,-1)$ and $x$-intercepts $(\pm1,0)$. The downward parabola has vertex $(0,2)$ and $x$-intercepts $(\pm\sqrt2,0)$.

spec.description: Oppositely opening parabolas with symmetric intersections and all axial intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=-(x-1)^2+1\\x^2&=-x^2+2x\\2x^2-2x&=0\\2x(x-1)&=0\\x&=0,\ 1\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=x^2$ gives $y=0,\ 1$ respectively.

The upward parabola has vertex $(0,0)$. The downward parabola has vertex $(1,1)$ and intercepts $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

spec.description: Upward and downward parabolas with labelled intersections and intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-x^2&=x^2+2x\\2x^2+2x&=0\\2x(x+1)&=0\\x&=0,\ -1\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=-x^2$ gives $y=0,\ -1$ respectively.

The first parabola opens downwards with vertex $(0,0)$. The second opens upwards with vertex $(-1,-1)$ and intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Downward parabola at the origin and upward parabola with vertex (-1,-1).

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x^2+4x&=(x+2)(x-1)\\2x^2+4x&=x^2+x-2\\x^2+3x+2&=0\\(x+1)(x+2)&=0\\x&=-1,\ -2\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=2x^2+4x$ gives $y=-2,\ 0$ respectively.

Both open upwards. The first has vertex $(-1,-2)$ and intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0)$. The second has vertex $(-\frac12,-\frac94)$, $x$-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(1,0)$, and $y$-intercept $(0,-2)$.

spec.description: Two upward parabolas with different widths and axes; all intercepts and intersections labelled.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-(x+2)(x-3)&=x^2-4\\-x^2+x+6&=x^2-4\\2x^2-x-10&=0\\(2x-5)(x+2)&=0\\x&=\frac52,\ -2\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=x^2-4$ gives $y=\frac{25}{4}-4=\frac94$ and $y=4-4=0$ respectively.

The downward parabola has $x$-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(3,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,6)$, and vertex $(\frac12,\frac{25}{4})$. The upward parabola has vertex $(0,-4)$ and $x$-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

spec.description: Oppositely opening parabolas with intersections (-2,0) and (5/2,9/4).

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)(x+2)&=-(x+2)(x+1)\\x^2+x-2&=-x^2-3x-2\\2x^2+4x&=0\\2x(x+2)&=0\\x&=0,\ -2\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=(x-1)(x+2)$ gives $y=-2,\ 0$ respectively.

The upward parabola has $x$-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(1,0)$ and vertex $(-\frac12,-\frac94)$. The downward parabola has $x$-intercepts $(-2,0)$ and $(-1,0)$ and vertex $(-\frac32,\frac14)$. Both have $y$-intercept $(0,-2)$.

spec.description: Oppositely opening parabolas sharing (-2,0) and (0,-2); all axial intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+x-6&=-x^2+5x-6\\2x^2-4x&=0\\2x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0,\ 2\end{align*}$$
Substitution into $y=x^2+x-6$ gives $y=-6,\ 0$ respectively.

The upward parabola has $x$-intercepts $(-3,0)$ and $(2,0)$ and vertex $(-\frac12,-\frac{25}{4})$. The downward parabola has $x$-intercepts $(2,0)$ and $(3,0)$ and vertex $(\frac52,\frac14)$. Both have $y$-intercept $(0,-6)$.

spec.description: Oppositely opening parabolas sharing (0,-6) and (2,0); all axial intercepts labelled.
